note.text: Industrialisation expands manufacturing capabilities and their links to the economy. Reliable electricity, skills, transport, finance and markets can support it. Where any of these is restricted, firms may face higher costs or uncertain output. These are conditions to investigate, not fixed qualities of a population. Resource exports can coexist with limited local processing.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to explain how a stated constraint can limit manufacturing and propose a relevant response. Builds on: inputs and agglomeration. Leads to: comparison with advanced industrial profiles.

sections.heading: Explain the geography
sections.text: Industrialisation expands manufacturing capabilities and their links to the economy. Reliable electricity, skills, transport, finance and markets can support it. Where any of these is restricted, firms may face higher costs or uncertain output. These are conditions to investigate, not fixed qualities of a population. Resource exports can coexist with limited local processing.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: In an invented processing business near Bafoussam, unreliable electricity interrupts machinery and poor roads delay inputs. Improved power reliability addresses one constraint; it does not automatically solve roads or finance. World Bank income groups measure income per person, not industrial structure. In its FY{2027} table Uganda is low income and Cameroon lower-middle income; neither label describes every factory.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Use a chain: constraint, effect on production, possible response, remaining limitation. Avoid treating income labels and industrial categories as interchangeable. Compare evidence within and between places.

a shortage of relevant technical capabilities
limited access to funds for viable equipment or working needs

mistake.why: Energy reliability can limit output independently of workers’ ability.

cards.idea: Distinguish the features before applying them.
example: power constraint: unreliable energy supply interrupting production.
transport constraint: cost or unreliability in moving inputs and outputs.
skills constraint: a shortage of relevant technical capabilities.
finance constraint: limited access to funds for viable equipment or working needs.

cards.idea: Use the evidence in the example, not a place name alone.
example: Machinery stops during outages in an invented workshop.
Inputs arrive late over an unreliable access route.
A firm cannot find technicians to maintain its equipment.
A processor cannot fund suitable machinery.

cards.idea: Explain how the process produces the stated effect.
example: Energy reliability can limit output independently of workers’ ability.
Production also depends on links beyond the factory.
Relevant training can help, but demand and other constraints remain.
Resources and accessible investment finance are different.

pick.q: A fictional machine repeatedly stops because supply voltage fails. Which response directly targets the stated constraint?
w: Change only the company logo
Assume workers are unwilling
Open an unrelated shop
e: A logo does not restore electricity.
The evidence identifies electricity, not motivation.
An unrelated shop does not power the machine.
pick.y: Match the intervention to the observed mechanism.

pick.q: A fictional processor lacks maintenance skills. Which proposal is most relevant?
pick.r: Train technicians for the actual equipment
w: Assume raw-material exports supply the skills
Measure only the number of roads
Declare every course equally useful
e: Exports do not automatically create maintenance capability.
Road counts do not identify technical skills.
Training relevance matters.
pick.y: Training should address the identified equipment and skill need.

pick.q: A report calls Cameroon a World Bank low-income country and treats that as a manufacturing measure. What correction is needed?
pick.r: The FY{2027} income label is lower-middle income; industrial structure requires separate evidence
w: Income and industry are identical measures
Every country has the same industrial structure
Only factory names determine income classification
e: Income groups and industrial measures answer different questions.
Industrial structures vary.
The income grouping uses income per person.
pick.y: Use the dated income classification accurately and assess industry separately.
